title: Minimum Number of Flips to Make Binary Grid Palindromic II
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix, determine the minimum number of cell flips required to make all rows and columns palindromic, ensuring the total number of 1's is divisible by 4.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix, determine the minimum number of cell flips required to make all rows and columns palindromic, ensuring the total number of 1's is divisible by 4.
constraints: grid is a nonempty rectangular binary matrix with at most 200,000 cells.
After flips, every row and column must be palindromic.
The final one count must be divisible by four; return the minimum flips.
hints: Both symmetries partition cells into four-cell orbits, middle pairs, and possibly a center.
Repair four-cell groups by majority, then resolve middle pairs modulo four and clear the center.
Count mismatched middle pairs and matched-one pairs; a mismatch can absorb parity, otherwise two extra flips may be needed.
Four-cell groups never alter the remainder; the pair parity rule is necessary and constructively sufficient.
editorial: Four-cell groups never alter the remainder; the pair parity rule is necessary and constructively sufficient.

tests.explanation: The corners form one orbit and the center must be zero; three flips satisfy every condition.
Two flips make all symmetry groups equal with a multiple of four ones.
